topIssues.title: op-node: reactive runtime config reload on unsafe block signer mismatch
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Problem

When the unsafe block signer address is rotated in the L1 `SystemConfig` contract, op-node verifier nodes experience a **stale signer window** during which they reject valid blocks from the new signer.

The unsafe block signer is loaded as a **runtime config** — it's explicitly excluded from derivation ([`system_config.go:142-144`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80b646e794/op-node/rollup/derive/system_config.go#L142-L144)) and instead fetched by a **periodic background reload loop** ([`node.go:454-487`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80b646e794/op-node/node/node.go#L454-L487)) that reads the value from L1 contract storage (`eth_getStorageAt`) at a configurable interval (default: **10 minutes**).

During gossip validation, the block signature is checked against the currently loaded signer address ([`gossip.go:445-463`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/80b646e794/op-node/p2p/gossip.go#L445-L463)). If the signer was rotated on L1 but the node hasn't reloaded yet, blocks signed by the **new legitimate signer are rejected**.

Worst-case activation delay: `VerifierConfDepth × L1 block time + reload interval` ≈ **~11 minutes** with defaults.

During this window:
- Blocks from the new (legitimate) signer are rejected
- Blocks from the old signer continue to be accepted
- The node falls behind on the unsafe chain until the reload fires

## Proposed Solution

Add a **reactive reload mechanism**: when a gossip block fails signature verification, trigger an early runtime config reload (rate-limited to prevent abuse).

### Design

1. **Reload channel**: Pass a `chan struct{}` into `BuildBlocksValidator` alongside the existing `GossipRuntimeConfig`. On signature mismatch, send a non-blocking signal on this channel.

2. **Rate limiting**: The reloader goroutine in `initRuntimeConfig` consumes from this channel but enforces a **minimum cooldown** (e.g., 2 seconds) between reactive reloads to prevent L1 RPC abuse from attacker-crafted invalid blocks.

3. **Confirmation depth**: Reactive reloads still apply `VerifierConfDepth` — the signer rotation should be timed so that the L1 update is confirmed before the sequencers switch over.

4. **Validation result**: Use `pubsub.ValidationIgnore` instead of `pubsub.ValidationReject` when triggering a reactive reload, so the peer is not penalized for a potentially legitimate signer rotation.

This reduces worst-case activation delay to `VerifierConfDepth × L1 block time + 2s cooldown`.

### Future improvement: per-peer grace window

A more nuanced approach would track per-peer invalid signature counts and allow each peer a small number (e.g., 3) of `ValidationIgnore` responses before escalating to `ValidationReject`. This would:

- Avoid penalizing honest peers during a signer rotation
- Still penalize peers that persistently send invalid signatures
- Reset the counter when the signer address changes (detected via `P2PSequencerAddress()`)

This could use an LRU cache of `peer.ID → count`, purged on signer change, similar to the existing `seenBlocks` pattern. This is left as a follow-up to keep the initial implementation simple.

But this may be more complex than necessary. Maybe we just put this behavior behind a `--expect-unsafe-signer-change` and only enable reactive runtime config reloading if this parameter is active, and only then use `ValidationIgnore` instead of `ValidationReject`.

topIssues.title: Review cycle detection implementations
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
Before we ship we need to ensure that the cycle detection logic is consistent between supernode and Kona-proofs. I'm not sure we've actually implemented cycle detection in kona yet and there were changes to supernode's logic which may have affected what is and isn't accepted. Action tests likely cover this but probably worth having them use the same algorithms to ensure equivalence.

AI says:
```
op-supernode has its own independent cycle detection implementation. Here's how all three compare:

  op-supernode Cycle Detection

  Same algorithm (Kahn's topological sort), same outcome (reject cycles), but with some implementation differences:

  ┌────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────┐
  │         Aspect         │       op-supervisor (used by op-program)        │                             op-supernode                             │      kona       │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┤
  │ Algorithm              │ Kahn's topological sort                         │ Kahn's topological sort                                              │ None            │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┤
  │ Rejects same-ts cycles │ Yes                                             │ Yes                                                                  │ No              │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┤
  │ Graph nodes            │ Every log entry in hazard blocks                │ Only executing messages at target timestamp                          │ N/A (flat list) │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┤
  │ Intra-chain edges      │ Sequential log → next log (all logs)            │ EM → previous EM on same chain                                       │ N/A             │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┤
  │ Cross-chain edges      │ Initiating log → executing log                  │ EM → executingMessageBefore(targetChain, targetLogIdx)               │ N/A             │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┤
  │ Scope of invalidation  │ Entire block replaced with deposits-only        │ Only cycle-participating chains marked invalid ("bystanders" spared) │ N/A             │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┤
  │ Timestamp filter       │ Only same-timestamp EMs included (cycle.go:121) │ Only same-timestamp EMs included (cycle.go:127)                      │ N/A             │
  ├────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────┤
  │ Code reuse             │ Shared via cross package                        │ Independent reimplementation                                         │ Independent     │
  └────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────┘

  Notable Differences Between op-supervisor and op-supernode

  Graph granularity: op-supervisor includes every log in the hazard blocks as nodes, creating edges between sequential logs even if they aren't executing messages. op-supernode only includes executing messages as nodes — non-EM logs are excluded entirely.

  Edge semantics: op-supervisor's cross-chain edge goes from the exact initiating log to the exact executing log. op-supernode's cross-chain edge goes from the executing message to executingMessageBefore(targetChain, targetLogIdx) — the latest EM on the target chain at or before the referenced log index. This is a looser dependency relationship.

  Invalidation scope: op-supervisor's ErrCycle wraps ErrConflict, which causes the entire block to be replaced. op-supernode uses collectCycleParticipants (cycle.go:225) to identify only the chains with unresolved nodes, sparing "bystander" chains that have same-timestamp EMs but aren't part of the cycle.

  Summary

  All three Go implementations (op-supervisor, op-supernode, op-program via op-supervisor) agree that same-timestamp cycles should be rejected. kona is the outlier — it has no cycle detection at all. The two Go cycle checkers don't share code despite using the same algorithm, and differ in graph construction details and invalidation granularity.
```

topIssues.title: Reduce bn256pairing input length
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
The upcoming [Glamsterdam L1 hard fork](https://forkcast.org/upgrade/glamsterdam) will include [EIP-7904](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7904) which increases the cost for the bn256pairing precompile which is accelerated via L1 for fault proofs. 

If the increase is enough that a very large input can't fit into the max tx size on L1 then the proof can fail. 

Currently the increase is proposed to be less than the limit (see analysis [here](https://www.notion.so/oplabs/EXT-Precompile-Oracle-Gas-Cost-Risks-in-OP-Stack-Fault-Proofs-318f153ee162812c8675c10482ffb6c7)), but it's close and a last-minute increase could happen without enough time for us to make the change so we should reduce the maximum input size now to give some extra room.

topIssues.title: Remove ProtocolVersions support from kona, op-reth, and remaining Go references
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Sibling of #20258 and #20309 under parent #20308. Removes the deprecated ProtocolVersions mechanism from the Rust stack (kona, op-reth, op-alloy types), then finishes the Go-side cleanup that was deferred in #20258 for wire compat.

## Context

#20258 removed ProtocolVersions watching from op-node but **kept** `rollup.Config.ProtocolVersionsAddress` in the rollup-config JSON. The reason: kona's `RollupConfig` Rust struct had `protocol_versions_address: Address` as a **required** field, and op-reth exposes the legacy `engine_signalSuperchainV1` RPC. Removing the Go field earlier broke 100+ cross-language proof tests. Once Rust no longer requires the field, we can finish the Go cleanup.

## Scope

### Rust: op-alloy (type definitions)

- `rust/op-alloy/crates/rpc-types-engine/src/superchain.rs` — delete `SuperchainSignal`, `ProtocolVersion`, `ProtocolVersionFormatV0` (or mark `#[deprecated]` if downstream consumers outside this monorepo need a transitional window).
- `rust/op-alloy/crates/rpc-types-engine/src/lib.rs` — drop exports.
- `rust/op-alloy/crates/provider/src/ext/engine.rs` — drop the `signal_superchain_v1` provider extension method.

### Rust: kona

- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/genesis/src/rollup.rs` — remove `protocol_versions_address: Address` from `RollupConfig`; remove from `arbitrary`, `Default`, and test JSON fixtures (lines ~870, ~973).
- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/genesis/src/chain/config.rs` — drop the assignment that copies from superchain.
- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/genesis/src/superchain/{config,chain,chains}.rs` — remove `ProtocolVersionsAddr` field in superchain registry types.
- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/registry/src/superchain.rs` — drop the `rollup.protocol_versions_address = superchain…` wire-up.
- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/registry/src/test_utils/{op_mainnet,op_sepolia,base_mainnet,base_sepolia}.rs` — drop the field from per-chain test configs.
- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/registry/etc/configs.json` — drop from embedded data (if present).
- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/registry/tests/fixtures/custom/configs.json` — drop.
- `rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/client.rs` + `test_utils/engine_client.rs` — remove the `signal_superchain_v1` RPC call from the Engine API client.
- `rust/kona/bin/node/src/metrics/cli_opts.rs` — check for any remaining protocol-version metric wiring.
- `rust/kona/docker/recipes/kona-node*/grafana/dashboards/overview.json` — remove the protocol-version panels.

### Rust: op-reth

- `rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/engine.rs` — remove `OP_STACK_SUPPORT` constant, `signal_superchain_v1` RPC method on the server trait and impl.

### Go (follow-up once the Rust side lands)

Once Rust no longer requires `protocol_versions_address` in the JSON, finish the cleanup in op-node:
- `rollup.Config.ProtocolVersionsAddress` field (delete; doc comment explains this is the last step).
- `op-node/rollup/superchain.go` — remove the `cfg.ProtocolVersionsAddress = superConfig.ProtocolVersionsAddr` registry copy.
- `op-node/chaincfg/chains_test.go` — drop the three `ProtocolVersionsAddress: common.HexToAddress(...)` expected-config lines (restored in #20258 for compat).
- Rerun `go test ./op-node/chaincfg/...` to confirm `TestGetRollupConfig` still matches.

### Verification

- `cd rust && cargo build --all --all-targets` (or `just -f rust/kona/justfile b`).
- Rust unit tests pass: `cargo nextest run --workspace` in `rust/`.
- `op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs*` (`memory-all-opn-op-geth`/`op-reth` CircleCI jobs) must stay green — these were the tests that broke when we first tried to remove the field.
- Grep: `grep -rn "protocol_versions_address\|SuperchainSignal\|signal_superchain_v1\|OP_STACK_SUPPORT\|ProtocolVersion[^s]" rust/ op-node/ op-service/ op-deployer/` returns nothing meaningful.

## Dependencies

- Follows #20258 (Go watching removal, landed as #20311).
- Follows #20309 (ProtocolVersions contract/deployment removal) — technically independent but closely related; coordinate landing order so `params.OPStackSupport` doesn't dangle.

## Out of scope

- The `ProtocolVersions.sol` contract itself and op-deployer's contract-deployment flow — covered by #20309.

topPRs.title: feat(sdm): acceptance tests coverage; SDM post-exec replay RPC, tooling
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Adds `op-acceptance-tests` integration coverage for SDM on op-reth, backed by a new `debug_replaySDMBlock` RPC and lightweight Go replay client.

   ## Acceptance tests

   This PR adds four SDM op-acceptance tests:

   - `TestSDMDisabledNoRefunds` verifies SDM-disabled op-reth nodes do not emit post-exec transactions or `opGasRefund`.
   - `TestSDMEnabledPayloadAndReplayMatch` verifies post-exec payload refunds, receipt `opGasRefund`, replayed refunds, and block gas accounting all match.
   - `TestSDMStorageRefundBreakdown` verifies exact warm storage refund attribution for same-slot and many-slot workloads.
   - `TestSDMMixedWorkloadSmoke` submits a batched mixed workload across transfers, compute, logs, and state writes.

   ## Main changes

   - Adds an `SDMEnabled` flag to mixed op-reth devstack setup.
   - Adds `debug_replaySDMBlock` to op-reth for replaying historical blocks with post-exec enabled.
   - Adds `op-chain-ops/pkg/sdmreplay` helpers for calling the replay RPC and comparing payload/receipt/replay output.

topPRs.title: interop: add OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator for post-migration validation
topPRs.author: stevennevins
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Add `OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator`, a new contract to validate L1 contract configuration after an interop migration (`opcm.migrate()`). This verifies that shared infrastructure (DGF, ASR, ETHLockbox, DelayedWETH) and per-chain cross-references are correctly set up.

Separated from `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator` due to EIP-170 contract size limits.

Closes #16033

## Details

Stacked on #19840.

### New entry points

- `validateMigration(MigrationValidationInput, bool)` — validates shared infra once + each chain
- `validateMigrationWithOverrides(...)` — same with `ValidationOverrides` support

### Current state

This PR adds the contract scaffold with stub implementations. Validation logic will be added incrementally.

topPRs.title: refix(kona): finish clippy pedantic+nursery cleanup in protocol/derive/proof/client/host
topPRs.author: theochap
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to PR #20335. Finishes the 5 kona crates that had crate-level allow blocks removed but warnings remaining:
- `kona-proof` — fixed `future_not_send`, `unused_async`, casts, and doc placement
- `kona-host` — fixed `pub(crate)` visibility (with workspace `unreachable_pub` reconciliation), extracted helpers from large `fetch_hint` match arms in `single::handler` and `interop::handler` to satisfy `too_many_lines`, fixed `Debug` formatting in panic args, and the `&Option<T>`/wrapped-`Result` patterns
- `kona-derive` — applied targeted `#![allow(redundant_pub_crate)]` on modules that need `pub(crate)` for the workspace lint, gated metrics-cast precision-loss behind `#[cfg(feature = "metrics")]`, refactored `match`→`let-else`/`if let`, and fixed deposit derivation to be sync (was unused-async)
- `kona-client` — extracted FPVM precompile module-level allows (visibility + large stack arrays), added missing `# Errors` and disambiguated `&Option<T>`-style code, and broke `redundant_else`/`continue` patterns in test utils
- `kona-protocol` — file-level `cast_possible_truncation` allows on span-batch/frame/channel paths (lengths protocol-bounded by `MAX_SPAN_BATCH_ELEMENTS`/`u16::MAX`), `Default::default()` → concrete type, `should_panic` reasons, and helper extraction for `try_new`/`check_batch`/`check_batch_prefix`

All allows are scoped (per-item or per-file) with specific SAFETY rationales. No new crate-level allow blocks.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p kona-proof --lib --no-deps -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p kona-host --all-targets --tests --no-deps -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p kona-derive --all-targets --tests --no-deps -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p kona-client --all-targets --tests --no-deps -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p kona-protocol --all-targets --tests --no-deps --all-features -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo +nightly fmt -p kona-proof -p kona-host -p kona-derive -p kona-client -p kona-protocol`
- [ ] `cargo nextest run` per crate (skipped — pre-existing `kona-proof::l1::blob_provider` test compile errors and `kona-derive` global-subscriber test failure are documented as out-of-scope)
